trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI (presumed unless the 164.402 four-factor assessment shows a low probability of compromise). Clock starts at discovery: the first day the breach is known, or by reasonable diligence would have been known, to the owner (164.404(a)(2))
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Each affected patient (first-class mail; substitute notice if 10 or more have out-of-date contact information)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - covered entity. Encrypted data is not unsecured PHI, which is why laptop encryption matters

obligation: HIPAA breach notice to HHS (500 or more)
deadline: Contemporaneously with individual notice (within 60 days of discovery)
notify: HHS Secretary via the OCR breach portal
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500+ (the practice has about 900 active patients, so a full patient-list theft would qualify)

obligation: HIPAA breach log to HHS (fewer than 500)
deadline: Within 60 days after the end of the calendar year
notify: HHS Secretary via the OCR breach portal

trigger: Breach affecting more than 500 residents of a state or jurisdiction
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 500 Florida residents

trigger: Law enforcement states that notice would impede an investigation
deadline: Delay for the period stated in writing; up to 30 days if the statement is oral and documented

obligation: Business associate breach notice to the practice (inbound)
trigger: The billing company, EHR vendor, cloud fax vendor, or IT consultant discovers a breach of the practice's PHI
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days after discovery (a BAA may set a shorter time)

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (includes medical history and treatment and health insurance identifiers)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach. A HIPAA-compliant notice is deemed compliant if the practice timely provides a copy of that notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - plan to the 30-day clock; counsel confirms the deemed-compliance path

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at one time
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely - about 900 active patients; recheck if former patients are affected and the count exceeds 1,000

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the practice (inbound)
trigger: A vendor maintaining a system for the practice has a breach of security
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, but no later than 10 days following the determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - applies to the billing company and other vendors that maintain systems for the practice

trigger: Affected patients who reside outside Florida
notify: Residents and regulators under each state's law

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
deadline: Before any payment; reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor

applies_at_this_tier: Only if coverage exists - no standalone cyber policy; check the professional liability policy for a cyber endorsement

applies_at_this_tier: No - the rule does not apply to HIPAA-covered entities (16 CFR 318.1(a))

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed only: 72 hours; 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; recheck when final
